claim: For the periodic four-qubit Heisenberg \(XX\) ring of Cao and Zhu with uniform field \(B\), nonzero exchange \(J\), temperature \(T>0\), and alternate-site concurrence \(C_{13}\), put \(x=|J|/T\), \(h=|B|/T\), \(a=\cosh(2x)\), \(k=\cosh(2\sqrt2\,x)\), and \(c=\cosh(2h)\). The concurrence sign is governed exactly by \[F_x(c)=L(x)c^2-Q(x)c-R(x),\]where \[L(x)=4\!\left(\sinh^4x-\cosh^2(\sqrt2\,x)\right),\quad Q(x)=4\cosh(2x)+2\cosh(2\sqrt2\,x)+2,\quad R(x)=(\cosh(2x)+1)^2.\]Let \(x_*>0\) be the unique solution of \(\sinh^2x_*=\cosh(\sqrt2\,x_*)\), numerically \(x_*=1.4195389207530749\ldots\), and let \(T_*=|J|/x_*=0.7044540909589808\ldots|J|\). If \(T\ge T_*\), then \(C_{13}=0\) for every finite \(B\). If \(0<T<T_*\), define \[c_*(x)=\frac{Q(x)+\sqrt{Q(x)^2+4L(x)R(x)}}{2L(x)},\qquad B_*(T)=\frac{T}{2}\operatorname{arcosh}c_*(|J|/T).\]Then \[\boxed{C_{13}(T,B)>0\iff |B|>B_*(T).}\]Thus at every subcritical positive temperature there is one lower field threshold and no finite upper field cutoff. Moreover \[B_*(T)\sim\sqrt2\,T\,e^{-(2-\sqrt2)|J|/T}\qquad(T\downarrow0),\]so the global lower-field floor is zero, while for fixed \(0<T<T_*\) \[C_{13}(T,B)\sim\left[\cosh(2|J|/T)-1-2\cosh(\sqrt2|J|/T)\right]e^{-2|B|/T}\qquad(|B|\to\infty).\]This exact positive-temperature phase diagram corrects the finite field-window impression in the source's numerical plots: the high-field entanglement becomes exponentially small but remains strictly positive at every sufficiently large finite field below \(T_*\).

scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the four-site periodic XX ring and alternate sites only.
The theorem is for strictly positive temperature; the zero-temperature phase diagram has separate ground-state level crossings.
The positive high-field concurrence is exponentially small and can underflow numerically.
Only abstract-level material was available for the closest later field-plus-DM paper, leaving a bounded originality risk.
title: Exact finite-temperature field phase diagram for alternate-site entanglement in the four-qubit XX ring
